title: Signal · Thursday 5 November
overview: The OCC's AI framework for US bank examiners, a reported valuation compromise in the UBS capital dispute and the markets' reaction to the Democrats' sweep of Congress lead this morning.

top.headline: OCC tells US bank examiners to judge AI by consequences, ranking payment agents highest
top.summary: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency issued a 22-page supervisory framework on 4 November for examiners reviewing banks' use of what the US government now calls super intelligence. AI is not to be treated as a separate risk category. Four illustrative tiers run from internal productivity tools up to Tier 1: autonomous payment agents, real-time credit decisions, fraud-hold release and market access.
top.background: Reuters says the OCC calls it the first guidance of its kind. It sets no new expectations for banks, though Reuters notes banks typically comply closely. It follows reports, less than two weeks ago, of unauthorised third-party agents in customer accounts at large US banks.
top.why: Banks now have a US benchmark for tiering AI use cases by reversibility, transfer of agency and human oversight. It also covers federal branches of foreign banks, so European groups with those licences are in scope.
top.watch_next: Whether the Federal Reserve and the FDIC publish matching guidance.

top.headline: Bloomberg: National Council member proposes valuation change to ease UBS capital dispute
top.summary: A member of the National Council has proposed that UBS value its foreign subsidiaries under the equity method, which could reduce its future capital needs, according to Bloomberg as reported by AWP. How much is unclear, and support is far from certain. UBS shares rose 4.0 percent on 4 November, amid fresh takeover rumours; UBS declined to comment.
top.background: In September the Council of States decided UBS must back foreign subsidiaries with 90 percent CET1 capital, about USD 16 billion extra according to AWP; the Federal Council's bill wanted full backing. UBS discussed this valuation approach in its February consultation response.
top.why: A change of method could keep the headline ratio while shrinking the amount, which gives parliament room to compromise and sets the tone for the wider too-big-to-fail package.
top.watch_next: The National Council's economic affairs committee debates the details on 23 and 24 November, ahead of the winter session.

top.headline: Democrats take Congress; Dow jumps 3 percent, Brent sinks and the SMI passes 15,000
top.summary: Democrats won majorities in both the House and the Senate in the 3 November midterms. On 4 November the Dow rose 1,569 points, or 3 percent, its best day since April 2025, while Brent fell almost 8.7 percent to USD 94.62 a barrel and Treasury yields and the dollar eased, CNN reported. In Zurich the SMI passed 15,000 points for the first time, according to SRF.
top.background: Traders priced in gridlock and possible de-escalation of the war with Iran, though Rapidan Energy Group's Bob McNally told CNN escalation is more likely. The AI trade went the other way: Nvidia fell 3 percent and CoreWeave roughly 10 percent as data centres became a campaign issue.
top.why: Higher equities and cheaper oil help wealth managers' assets and change the client conversation on dollar exposure. For buyers of AI, a political question now hangs over data centre capacity.
top.watch_next: Whether Democratic wins in states such as Texas lead to moratoriums or limits on data centres.

items.headline: Crédit Mutuel Arkéa confirms cyberattack as investigator traces USD 133 million to crypto
items.summary: The French banking group said on 4 November that an attack enabled fraudulent transactions, that it is contained and that customers will lose nothing. It has not confirmed the amount: blockchain investigator ZachXBT estimates more than USD 133 million, moved through stablecoins. French reports link the fraud to Fortuneo, its online bank; the entry point is unknown.
items.why: Transfers reportedly matched the names on crypto exchange accounts opened with fake identities, so banks should test whether name-matching controls catch this pattern.

items.headline: Capgemini: 59 percent of financial firms try multi-agent AI, 10 percent orchestrate it enterprise-wide
items.summary: The Capgemini Research Institute's World Cloud Report for Financial Services 2027, published on 5 November and based on 1,100 C-suite executives, finds 59 percent piloting or deploying multi-agent AI. Roughly half cannot consistently show a return on agentic AI, and 90 percent use or plan intelligent model routing to manage token costs.
items.why: A benchmark for bank steering committees: eight in ten executives prioritise cutting tech debt and 52 percent prefer hyperscalers to govern agents, which raises concentration questions.

items.headline: TWINT now lets Swiss users pay QR bills in its app and schedule them
items.summary: TWINT said on 4 November that customers can scan the Swiss QR code on a bill, check the details and set a payment date within the due period. A payment button and an upload option cover digital bills. Issuers change nothing because it builds on the existing standard; first users include Planzer Paket, EKS, EWL and green.ch.
items.why: Moves TWINT onto ground held by e-banking and eBill, so Swiss retail banks should watch whether bill payments, and the customer contact they bring, shift to the app.

items.headline: Vaud's cantonal insurer ECA writes off CHF 12.9 million on software never deployed
items.summary: ECA Vaud booked a CHF 12.9 million impairment in its 2025 accounts for SI Assurance, a system for some 639,000 policies, according to ICTjournal, citing 24 heures. The initial 2020 contract with Inetum, then GFI, was CHF 5.59 million. ECA blames repeated delays; Inetum says the software was in final acceptance and has gone to court.
items.why: A caution for Swiss insurers and banks replacing old core systems: once integration and internal costs were counted, the write-off reached more than twice the initial contract.

items.headline: Salesforce says Agentforce Coworker passes 185,000 users, with Fulton Bank among adopters
items.summary: Salesforce said on 4 November that Coworker usage grew 21 times in three months and that more than 185,000 people now use it. New features include reusable Skills, conversation history and access from Microsoft Teams, mobile and desktop. It costs USD 50 per user per month.
items.why: A fixed per-seat price for delegated agents gives banks on Salesforce a simple cost comparison against token-metered tools.

items.headline: Federal Council lifts BVG minimum rate to 2.0 percent from 2027; insurers object
items.summary: The Federal Council raised the minimum interest rate on occupational pension savings from 1.25 to 2.0 percent from January 2027, above the 1.75 percent its pension commission recommended, citing pension funds' solid finances and inflation since 2022, finews reported on 4 November. The Swiss Insurance Association says 1.0 percent would have been appropriate.
items.why: Raises the cost of guarantees for pension providers with full guarantee promises, which is why insurers object, and sets a higher return bar for BVG mandates.

items.headline: Swiss franc bond issuance hits CHF 89 billion, already matching the 2009 record
items.summary: Bonds with a nominal value of CHF 89 billion reached the Swiss primary market by the end of October, level with the CHF 88.9 billion of 2009, finews reported on 4 November, using Zürcher Kantonalbank statistics. October's CHF 7.3 billion, excluding Confederation bonds, was the highest for that month. Foreign borrowers added only CHF 800 million.
items.why: A strong year for the capital markets desks at Swiss banks, while thin foreign issuance suggests global uncertainty has reached the franc market.

items.headline: DWS adopts Deutsche Asset Management brand and coordinates family offices from Switzerland
items.summary: DWS is introducing Deutsche Asset Management as its global umbrella brand from early November to March 2027, DWS Switzerland chief executive Sven Württemberger told finews; DWS and Xtrackers stay as product brands. He takes on worldwide coordination of the family office business from Switzerland, with closer cooperation across Deutsche Bank's investment and private banking.
items.why: A second big European manager targets Swiss family offices after AllianzGI in October, adding competition for private banks in that client group.

items.headline: Revolut reaches USD 115 billion valuation in secondary sale as US bank nears
items.summary: Investors including Glade Brook, Coatue, Durable, T. Rowe Price and Baillie Gifford completed a secondary share sale valuing Revolut at USD 115 billion, 53 percent above a year ago, TechCrunch reported on 4 November. No new money went into the company. It plans to launch a US bank in the first half of 2027, subject to final approval.
items.why: Each new licence widens Revolut's reach into retail and SME banking, and its plan for a Swiss bank licence makes that a local question too.

items.headline: Starling chief executive Raman Bhatia plans to leave after two years, FT reports
items.summary: Raman Bhatia, chief executive of UK digital bank Starling, has privately told the board he no longer wants to run the bank, according to the Financial Times, as reported by PYMNTS on 4 November. The board has stepped up succession plans amid flagging growth. Starling declined to comment.
items.why: Set against Revolut's valuation on the same day, it shows how far the UK challengers have diverged, with Starling still dealing with FCA restrictions dating from 2021.

items.headline: OpenAI says agents built 948 Linux root exploits, with patches, for USD 1.2 million
items.summary: OpenAI said on 4 November that one pipeline run reproduced 1,724 Linux kernel vulnerabilities and produced 948 validated privilege escalation exploits with candidate patches, at USD 1,213,430 in API credits, according to RuntimeWire and Startup Fortune. The patches have not yet shipped to the kernel; OpenAI is working with maintainers, with human review first.
items.why: If a root exploit costs about USD 1,279, banks running Linux should expect shorter gaps between kernel changes and working attacks, and faster patch cycles from vendors.

items.headline: Apple reportedly cuts engineers' daily AI cap from USD 300 to USD 200
items.summary: Apple lowered the daily AI spending cap for engineering teams from USD 300 to USD 200 in October, with some allowances falling to USD 100, and is weighing a limit as low as USD 25 a day outside engineering, according to Bloomberg, as reported by TechCrunch on 4 November. TechCrunch had asked Apple for comment.
items.why: Token budgets are becoming a line to manage, so bank AI business cases should set per-user consumption limits from the start.

items.headline: Uber saw four agent-booked rides among about 320 million weekly trips and orders
items.summary: Uber said on its third-quarter earnings call on 4 November that only four rides and 500 Uber Eats orders came through AI agents in the week of Halloween, its busiest in October, out of around 320 million trips and orders. Chief executive Dara Khosrowshahi called the traction very limited. DoorDash has reported only a few hundred agent orders so far.
items.why: Consumer agent traffic is still tiny even as supervisors write rules for it, so banks have time to build agent identity and payment controls before volumes arrive.

items.headline: OpenAI agrees to buy Pierre for Codex; Meta buys coding start-up Conductor
items.summary: OpenAI said on 4 November it will acquire Pierre Computer Company, whose Code Storage offers Git hosting built for software agents, and fold it into Codex; terms were not disclosed and the deal has not closed. The same day Meta confirmed it bought Conductor, which runs coding agents in parallel workspaces, TechCrunch reported.
items.why: The labs are buying the layers around the coding model, so firms standardising on one agent stack should check where their code and agent memory will live.

items.headline: Apache Spark 4.3 brings stateful real-time streaming under 150 ms to Databricks Runtime 19
items.summary: Databricks said on 5 November that Apache Spark 4.3, now in Databricks Runtime 19, adds streaming aggregation, deduplication and custom stateful processing to Real-Time Mode, with sub-150 ms P99 latency in three benchmarks. It also adds SCD Type 2 history tracking through Python, SQL and Spark Connect.
items.why: Fraud detection, an example Databricks gives, could run on the engine banks already use for batch and AI, and built-in history helps with reporting and audit.
items.for_your_skills: For your skills: Architecture & TOM can treat low-latency stateful streaming as part of Spark for supported workloads, without a separate streaming engine.

say_it_today: The OCC puts the autonomous payment agent in its top risk tier, while Uber counted four agent-booked rides in a week of about 320 million trips and orders. Supervisors are setting the terms before the traffic arrives, which makes now the cheap moment to build agent identity and payment controls.
